definition: Movement therapy is a therapeutic approach that uses dance or movement to help improve mental and physical functioning.

provenance.scope: Source record C205543; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports a health professional (Dance Therapist), not the therapy itself, so the definition targets the wrong sense of the term.

“Therapeutic approach that uses dance or movement” is broader and differently framed than the supplied source text, which only states that the professional uses dance/movement therapy to improve mental and physical function.
The field label is not the main issue, but the definition should be supported by the packet’s wording and sense; here it is not.

The packet content supports that a dance/movement therapy practitioner uses dance/movement therapy to improve mental and physical function, but it does not support that this is a “therapeutic approach” in the abstract (it describes an occupation/discipline: “A health professional who uses dance/movement therapy…”).
The definition is placed in the cognition field, but the packet does not link movement therapy to cognition specifically—only to mental and physical function more generally.
